blocks.text: The verb "to carry" in Russian is rendered in two ways depending upon the way of carrying: on foot — носить-нести, понести; by vehicle — возить-везти, повезти. Note that these verbs directly correspond in their usage to the "going verbs" ходить-идти, пойти and ездить-ехать, поехать.

Note some special uses of these verbs: нести ответственность — to bear responsibility; нести потери — to suffer casualties; носить костюм (пальто, шляпу, ботинки etc.) — to wear (habitually); носить очки — to wear glasses.

Note also the following idiomatic construction: Мне не везёт. — I am not lucky. Ему везёт. — He is lucky. Вам повезло. — You were lucky. The "carrying verbs" (just like the "going verbs") form their perfectives by adding the prefix "по-" to the actual function verbs.
Водить — вести: to lead, to take, to drive, to conduct

This verb also follows the pattern of "going verbs". Note the following meanings: 1. to lead, to take: Я веду моего сына в школу. Я каждый день вожу его в школу. 2. to drive: Кто ведёт эту машину? Он не умеет водить машину. 3. to conduct: Противник ведёт огонь. 4. to behave oneself: Этот мальчик плохо ведёт себя. Note that in the last two examples (3 and 4) only the actual function verb "вести" can be used. (Never "водить").

Three pairs of motion verbs generally refer to 'taking', 'leading' with additional lexical information on manner of motion and object of transport encoded in the verb stem. These are нести/носить, вести/водить, and везти/возить.

items: Она несёт домашнее задание на занятия.

exercises.why: **носит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **носить** (to carry, to bear (a burden)) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **нести** for one direction. present: я ношу́ · ты но́сишь · он но́сит · мы но́сим · вы но́сите · они но́сят. — Wiktionary, «носить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verb "to carry" in Russian is rendered in two ways depending upon the way of carrying: on foot — носить-нести, понести; by vehicle — возить-везти, повезти.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  «to carry (on foot) — repeated function: носить — ношу, -сишь; носил; буду носить; actual function: нести — несу, -ёшь; нёс; буду нести; perfective: понести — понёс; понесу, -ёшь.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  «Note some special uses of these verbs: нести ответственность — to bear responsibility; нести потери — to suffer casualties; носить костюм (пальто, шляпу, ботинки etc.) — to wear (habitually); носить очки — to wear glasses.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  «иногда» marks a repeated or habitual action, which is the job of the many-directions verb.  Compare: «Он носит портфель.» (He carries a briefcase.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Она несёт домашнее задание на занятия.» (She is taking her assignment to class.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **несёт** is from **нести**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). Compare: «Учитель вёл школьников на экскурсию.» (The teacher was taking the children to a field trip.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Она водила свою подругу в театр.» (She took her friend to the theatre.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Том ___ (нести — to carry on foot, one way) белую коробку.
exercises.why: **нёс** is the past tense (masculine) of **нести** (to bear, to bring, to carry) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **носить** for many directions. past: он нёс · она несла́ · оно несло́ · они несли́. — Wiktionary, «нести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verb "to carry" in Russian is rendered in two ways depending upon the way of carrying: on foot — носить-нести, понести; by vehicle — возить-везти, повезти.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  «to carry (on foot) — repeated function: носить — ношу, -сишь; носил; буду носить; actual function: нести — несу, -ёшь; нёс; буду нести; perfective: понести — понёс; понесу, -ёшь.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  Compare: «Она несёт домашнее задание на занятия.» (She is taking her assignment to class.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Он носит портфель.» (He carries a briefcase.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
